## Design

### 2026-10-12 – My CAD journey begins today!

**2h**

My CAD journey begins today!

I started off the day by learning how to use CAD software. I've decided to go with Onshape since it's free and browser-based, and also because the Hack Club tutorials often use it. Thus I figured I'd have the best chance of getting help from the community/slack.

After getting to grips with Onshape, I designed this monstrosity:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/EBuChAcUkspX5zhs3qEVPUNL9stbHepB/8067fac19d72aea9de9e01166c9e6782da066af0d2324fd6adc0e3d028de37b3.png)
It's a very rough demo of the shell I'm going to make. I also designed a few weird bits and shapes but ultimately deleted them to make way for this cleaner box shape.

I thought then that I might just launch into modelling the final thing, but stopped myself. I know that I need a good plan to make something half decent, especially as I have to get this thing right first try. So, I took lots of measurements, using LCSC datasheets for accurate part dimensions (W LCSC datasheets), and whipped up this sketch of the box top plate:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/EBuChAcUkspX5zhs3qEVPUNL9stbHepB/b36c931193232148734696f1dcd75203e57d97127a0a61db7b19dbe480a4dafe.png)

So there is how it looks, and what I've made so far! I just need to plan out the sides of the box, and then I can move on to starting to 3D model the whole thing, making sure I stick to my measurements and plans precisely!

Side note: why does the Onshape viewer always have to be tilted so wonkily all the time? L Tung can't lie

### 2026-10-13 – I started today by finalising my plans. My planning document is now very big, as pictured! I have decided how to mount the PCB (M3 holes through it) and the top plate of the box (pillars through the P

**2h**

I started today by finalising my plans. My planning document is now very big, as pictured! I have decided how to mount the PCB (M3 holes through it) and the top plate of the box (pillars through the PCB) and made holes in the PCB accordingly. I have worked out the dimensions of those holes, too.
I then started modelling! It takes me a long time to do everything since I'm not very confident with it yet, and I've had to redo things so many times because they secretly cause problems and don't do what you thought they did!

### 2026-10-14 – So, turns out I had got my maths wrong in a few places. Measuring from inconsistent points on the circles can't have helped... anyway, I changed the box to be centred around the origin, and redid the

**1h**

So, turns out I had got my maths wrong in a few places. Measuring from inconsistent points on the circles can't have helped... anyway, I changed the box to be centred around the origin, and redid the circles, measuring consistently this time. And when I brought in a 3D model of the PCB, they lined up perfectly! So now I just have to make the cutout for the USB port in the side, and then the top plate.

I have also figured out  how to not make the top plate look so stupid. I saw last night this picture of Hack Club's Meghana's macro pad and realised just before i went to sleep how I can make it look better. All I have to do is make the box wider than the actual PCB, and then make the top plate have wide edges to match! Then it looks like the PCB is that wide and it won't look stupid! I can have nice cutouts for the keys etc and a good 10mm bezel. So I adjusted my model and plans for that, and tomorrow, I'll start doing the top plate too!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/EBuChAcUkspX5zhs3qEVPUNL9stbHepB/78a9c5026b9aba8322b7952fa5e869c0ee4f7af4255273b92073fee685e16ec4.png)

### 2026-10-16 – Today I have now finally got the holes in the right place... except I've just realised that they need to be pillars, not holes in a flat base. Because I'm using through-hole components. So, I'll quick

**1.2h**

Today I have now finally got the holes in the right place... except I've just realised that they need to be pillars, not holes in a flat base. Because I'm using through-hole components. So, I'll quickly fix that tomorrow.

I have also put the cutout for the USB in. This sent me down a bit of a rabbit hole, since I realised I had forgotten headers for the Pi Pico. So, I found some of those and then could work out the correct height for the hole. But this meant that I had to make the walls taller too (to 3cm high now).

So it's looking really good, and I've just got the top plate to do now!

(holes need to be pillars now but that's fine I can just reverse the extrude):

### 2026-10-16 – Made some more good progress today. I have spent some time researching threaded inserts and screws to decide which to use. I have then adjusted my plan slightly as I realised I wouldn't have space und

**1.4h**

Made some more good progress today. I have spent some time researching threaded inserts and screws to decide which to use. I have then adjusted my plan slightly as I realised I wouldn't have space under the through hole components. Or did i say that already? cant remember lol. Anyway, I have now gone for 3 pillars with holes cut out for the threaded inserts. And after re-adding the holes to the PCB (they somehow vanished) and adjusting the position of one to be further away from a pillar, the box is done! So now I just need to model the lid, which will attach with magnets.

### 2026-10-17 – BIG PROGRESS TODAY!

**2.1h**

BIG PROGRESS TODAY!

I have officially finished 3D modelling the enclosure! Wow, that was hard. I have really been using ALL of my brain for this. But, I think I have something that will be almost perfect. And if it isn't... well, thank goodness I have files and sandpaper!

I started by making a lip for the magnets to sit in. Then made the holes for those magnets.
Then I moved on to the lid. This went much faster now I have all my measurements already worked out. I added cutouts for all the components (the 3D model of the PCB and of a keycap were very useful), and gave the edges some nice rounded corners. Then added the holes for the magnets.

I brought both parts into an assembly view, and lined them up. Everything was in the right place and the magnet holes lined up! So, tomorrow, I just have to prep the model for printing, figure out exactly where I'm going to get all my components, and budget it. Then submit!

### 2026-10-18 – THE ENCLOSURE IS DONE!

**2.68h**

THE ENCLOSURE IS DONE!

Yeah, there was no way I would be able to make a screen enclosure as well this week (neither time or budget lol).

This was a rather humbling experience - I had no idea just how hard CAD would be! I thought my limited blender skills would translate, but not really.

Today, I started checking the price with different 3DP manufacturers. However, JLC3DP (the cheapest!) wouldn't FDM print my top plate because it was under the 10mm thickness limit (it's 5). So, I went back to Onshape to see if there was anything I could do about it. That's when I suddenly thought, oh, I'd better check how far up the keycaps stick through the top plate. So I brought in a Cherry MX Switch 3D model and a keycap 3D model and put them in position on the PCB. And that's when I realised the keycaps barely poked up above the top of the lid.

It turns out that while trying to make the enclosure tall enough to have 8.5mm sockets for the microcontroller, I had made the entire thing far too tall. After a lot of thinking and some remodelling, I realised that I just had to do away with the sockets and solder the microcontroller directly onto the PCB. So I remodelled the height of the box and completely changed how the USB cutout would work so that now it goes through the box and the lid, and did a bunch more changes, and after all that, the box is finally done once again. Everything fits and everything should now be good. Fingers crossed.

So I uploaded the files to JLC3DP and got a quote which was surprisingly reasonable. Way cheaper than local or independent ones, including shipping cost, which is really crazy. Thank you, JLC3DP, and thank you, China.

 The lid is going to be printed out of resin because I didn't want to make it 10mm thick. And I'm not screwing anything into the lid, so resin should be fine. And the base will be printed out of PLA because, yeah, I would have preferred to have gone with ABS or ASA, but they were like three times the price.

Then finalised my threaded inserts and magnets. Now I just need to go hunting for some non-countersunk M3 6mm screws, and buy some if I don't have any!

And that is my week 2 project finished!
